financing.summary: Not a conventional for-sale homebuilder: Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is a nonprofit whose independent local affiliates buy land, build and sell the homes; HFHI itself holds no homebuilding land and has no lot-option programme. It is not a plausible land-banking customer in the conventional sense: there is no central land buyer or takedown pipeline, homes are sold at affordable prices to lower-income buyers, and land capital is philanthropic or concessionary. HFHI funds affiliates' land through its wholly owned CDFI, Habitat Capital ($46.8M lent to 31 affiliates in FY2026), and the US Property Acquisition Fund, an $82.5M vehicle launched March 2025 that borrows at 2% to 6.01% from JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Enterprise Community Loan Fund and foundations and on-lends to affiliates for land and property purchases. Consolidated borrowings were about $110M at June 30, 2026 ($57.1M notes payable, $52.9M investor notes backed by affiliate notes), against $767M of total assets. Any opening for a land banker would be one-off deals with individual large affiliates, or learning from the Property Acquisition Fund structure, not a corporate relationship with HFHI.
financing.land_strategy: HFHI owns no homebuilding land (land, buildings and equipment were $5.0M net at June 30, 2026). Each independent affiliate sources and holds its own land. HFHI supports them with acquisition, predevelopment and construction loans from Habitat Capital and the US Property Acquisition Fund, plus grants; there is no stated owned/optioned target and no lot-option structure.

lots.source_title: HFHI consolidated financial statements, June 30, 2026 and 2025
lots.note: No lot count is published at network or HFHI level. Affiliates' land sits on each affiliate's own balance sheet and is not consolidated into HFHI.

land_banking.counterparty: US Property Acquisition Fund, LLC (HFHI subsidiary; fund manager Enterprise Community Loan Fund)
land_banking.description: In-house substitute for a land banker: an $82.5M fund run through Habitat Capital that lends to U.S. Habitat affiliates and mission-aligned entities to buy land and property. It is a loan fund, not a lot-option arrangement. Target is about 1,000 additional homes, a 5% lift on a 3,482-unit baseline.
land_banking.source_title: Habitat for Humanity International announces new partnership to invest $82.5 million in affordable housing
land_banking.note: Class A lenders: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Enterprise Community Loan Fund. Class B: ImpactAssets, Arnold Ventures, Annie E. Casey Foundation, plus HFHI equity. Larson Foundation seed funding. The FY2026 audit caps fund borrowings at $72.5M and shows $52.1M drawn at June 30, 2026 (up from $24.2M a year earlier). A JPMorgan-sponsored Commercial Observer piece (2025-06-16) puts JPMorgan's commitment at $30M and the average projected home price at $300,000.

land_banking.counterparty: Habitat Capital, LLC (HFHI's wholly owned CDFI, formerly Habitat Mortgage Solutions)
land_banking.description: Lends to affiliates for land acquisition, predevelopment, construction, mini-perm, bridge and working capital, and runs New Markets Tax Credit allocations and a mortgage origination platform. FY2026: $46.8M closed in 33 loans to 31 affiliates in 20 states.
land_banking.source_title: Habitat for Humanity International FY2026 Annual Report
land_banking.note: Habitat Capital balance sheet per the annual report: total assets $153.3M, liabilities $123.2M, net assets $30.2M at FY2026. Loan volume by year: FY2023 $11.9M, FY2024 $30.9M, FY2025 $33.5M, FY2026 $46.8M. Example on the Habitat Capital page: a $1.85M acquisition loan to Austin Habitat for 30 home sites. An 'Enterprise Line of Credit' pilot gives multi-project financing to affiliates.

capital_events.description: US Property Acquisition Fund borrowings more than doubled in FY2026, from $24.2M to $52.1M across Class A and Class B lenders, with three new Class A lenders added. Over the same year HFHI's affiliate notes receivable rose from $54.6M to $81.0M.

capital_events.description: US Property Acquisition Fund missed one financial covenant (loan loss reserve account) at June 30, 2026, which the audit attributes to timing after funding two lines of credit that day; extra reserves were funded after year end and the covenant was brought back into compliance.

capital_events.description: Habitat Capital launched a $15M pilot fund of subordinate, unsecured, equity-like revolving credit for nonprofit developers and affiliates, piloted in California and New Jersey: $10M from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, $3M from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, $2M from Habitat Capital. Stated aim is a $50M to $100M national fund within two years.
capital_events.source_title: Habitat Capital launches pilot fund to address financing challenges for nonprofit real estate developers
capital_events.note: This is the equity-gap product: it fills the guarantee and equity shortfall that stops affiliates from getting senior construction and land loans.

Casey Foundation and HFHI equity in Class B.

key_metrics.source_title: HFHI consolidated financial statements, June 30, 2026 and 2025 (audit report dated November 17, 2026, Grant Thornton)

gaps: How to read the key metrics: Total debt = notes payable $57.1M + investor notes payable $52.9M (excludes leases and the $143.7M GGRF programme advance). Cash is unrestricted cash and equivalents ($58.2M a year earlier); a further $266.4M is restricted cash ($143.7M GGRF, $122.7M other) and $274.7M is investments. Liquidity is the audit's figure for financial assets available for general expenditure within one year ($119.4M a year earlier), before the undrawn $10M line. Total assets $767.3M, net assets $452.1M, FY2026 revenue $393.7M, expenses $382.9M. No public credit rating found.
Lot counts (owned, optioned, controlled): not published. Land sits with the independent affiliates and is not consolidated or reported at network level.

Named land banker or lot-option partner: none. No public link to Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon appears in HFHI's FY2026 audit, annual report or fund releases; a wider press search could not be run because the swarm's web-search allowance was used up.
Investor notes payable ($52.9M): investors not named.
$10M line of credit: bank, pricing and covenants not disclosed.
$5.0M non-interest-bearing performance-based note: lender and maturity not disclosed.

US Property Acquisition Fund: loan terms to affiliates (rate, tenor, advance rate), number of loans made and acres or lots financed are not publicly disclosed. One example seen only in a search snippet: a $1.19M loan to Habitat Wake County for 4.5 acres (not confirmed on an opened page).
Habitat Capital's own funding lines (the $123.2M of liabilities on its stand-alone balance sheet) are not broken out by lender beyond what the consolidated audit shows.
Credit ratings: none found in the documents opened; SEC EDGAR was not checked (nonprofit, not an SEC registrant as far as the audit shows).
M&A: none found for HFHI in 2025 to 2026. It is a nonprofit federation and does not acquire builders; mergers between local affiliates happen but were not tracked.

Network-level financing (affiliates' own bank lines, bond issues, mortgage sales) is outside HFHI's statements. HFHI's release puts federated network revenue at about $3.4B for FY2026 against HFHI's own $393M.

U.S. new-home count for FY2026 is not stated in households in the documents opened: the annual report gives 16,364 individuals served by new and rehab construction in the U.S. and Canada, using a four-people-per-household conversion.
